SPEC COMPLIANCE CHUNK FP-11: FHIRPath — §5.7 Math (STU). Test these items: abs(), ceiling(), exp(), floor(), ln(), log(base), power(exponent), round([precision]), sqrt(), truncate(). For DuckDB-backed FHIRPath/CQL surfaces, test both the native/C++ extension path and the Python fallback where both exist, and compare outputs between paths. For SQL-on-FHIR ViewDefinition chunks, test parser validation, SQL generation, DuckDB execution, and official spec fixtures/examples relevant to the chunk.

When the pipeline is fully complete, set workflow to null, set exit_reason, write all handoff files, and return control to the outer spec compliance orchestrator.

issues.spec_citation: FHIRPath N1 2.0.0 §5.7 power(exponent): 'If this function is used with Integers, the result is an Integer'; STU3 functions.json: both-integer negative exponent -> empty
issues.evidence: Both engines: 2.power(3).toString()='8.0', type Decimal (test_math_parity.py:211-214 pins it); (0-2).power(-3)=-0.125, 10.power(-1)=0.1 (should be empty: unrepresentable Integer). Probe .temp/qa/probe2.py
issues.root_cause: fn_power (evaluator.cpp) and invocations/math.py power() always produced Decimal-typed results; the §5.7 Integer-in/Integer-out typing rule and the STU3 negative-Integer-exponent-empty rule were not implemented (old pin test_math_parity.py:211-214 even asserted Decimal).
issues.resolution: Both engines: Integer base + Integer exponent -> int64 Integer result (plain rendering); beyond int64 degrades to exact Decimal-shaped text; negative Integer exponent on Integer base -> empty. test_math_parity pins updated; new test_power_math_fp11_skeptic.py.
issues.verified_in: Iteration 2 verification pass (0 divergences across probe_fp11/probe2; 40/40 focused tests; conformance 2832/2832)

issues.evidence: Native std::pow leaks binary64 noise for Decimal bases: 1.1.power(2) N=1.2100000000000002 vs P=1.21; 0.1.power(3) N=0.0010000000000000002 vs P=0.001; 10.power(-1) N=0.10000000000000001 vs P=0.1. Native exact path only covers integer-text bases (powerIntegerExactText).
issues.root_cause: Native fn_power used std::pow (binary64) for Decimal-text bases and negative integral exponents, leaking representation noise; only integer-text bases had an exact path.
issues.resolution: New powerDecimalExactText (+ roundDecimalTextHalfEvenSig, divideIntegerMagnitudeText) computes exact string-magnitude powers, places the decimal point, and renders 28-sig ROUND_HALF_EVEN like the Python Decimal context; pure integer bases keep full exact digits (FP-11 EXPLORER doctrine). Extension rebuilt + redeployed (repo bundle, site-packages, ~/.duckdb/v1.5.2).
issues.verified_in: Iteration 2 verification pass (0 divergences across probe_fp11/probe2; 40/40 focused tests; conformance 2832/2832)

issues.evidence: Python fallback (0-0.4).round() -> '-0.0' vs native '0.0' (negative zero Decimal from quantize).
issues.root_cause: Python fallback rround() quantize produced Decimal('-0') for tie-free negatives in (-0.5,0], serialized as '-0.0'.
issues.resolution: Normalize negative zero to Decimal 0 via copy_abs() when result == 0.
issues.verified_in: Iteration 2 verification pass (0 divergences across probe_fp11/probe2; 40/40 focused tests; conformance 2832/2832)

issues.spec_citation: FHIRPath §5.7 sqrt(): 'equivalent to raising to power 0.5'; §5.7 transcendental shortest-round-trip rendering doctrine (FP-11 HISTORIAN 2026-06-28)
issues.root_cause: Python fallback pow(Decimal, Decimal) rendered non-integral-exponent results at 28 digits while native std::pow rendered shortest-round-trip binary64.
issues.resolution: Python power() routes non-integral exponents through math.pow(float) (inf/nan -> empty); native std::pow fallthrough now sets normalizeDecimalMathSourceText shortest-round-trip source_text (fixed notation).
issues.verified_in: Iteration 2 verification pass (0 divergences across probe_fp11/probe2; 40/40 focused tests; conformance 2832/2832)

issues.evidence: Launch brief said round() half-even; verified normative text (N1 2.0.0 + STU3 master functions.json): traditional round, 0.5->1 and -0.5->-1. Existing ROUND_HALF_UP impl correct. exp/ln/log/sqrt render binary64 shortest-round-trip on BOTH engines by deliberate pin; launch's '28-digit half-even' applies to rational/UCUM conversions, not transcendentals. INTENDED, no change.

Residual divergence on non-integral-exponent power with small results, e.g. (0.001).power(1.37): native std::pow inside the extension returns a double <=1 ULP from libm pow used by Python math.pow, so native renders 0.000077624711663 (11-sig shortest for ITS double) vs fallback 0.00007762471166286911. Pre-existing ULP-class drift (old code documented the same as QA-006 LOW drift); both renderings faithful to their own double; agreeing to 10+ significant digits. Not chased: would require a correctly-rounded pow implementation.
